html:
A single stone arch bridge over the Neretva river at Mostar, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, finished in 1566 under the Ottomans.

Suleiman the Magnificent ordered it to replace a wooden bridge. The builder was Mimar Hayruddin, a pupil of the great architect Sinan. Its arch spans about 29 metres and rises high above the water. The town took its name from the bridge keepers, the mostari. For centuries young men have dived from it into the cold river.

On 9 November 1993, during the Bosnian War, Croat forces shelled it until it fell into the river. Its loss became a symbol of the destruction of the shared Ottoman heritage of Bosnia's Muslims, Croats and Serbs. It was rebuilt with stone from the same quarry and old methods, and reopened in 2004. UNESCO listed the old town in 2005.
sum: A single stone arch bridge over the Neretva river at Mostar, in Bosnia and Herzegovina, finished in 1566 under the Ottomans.
